Distinction internationale pour l'Algéri: International distinction for Algeria at WSIS 2026
ALGER, 11/07/2026 (Algeria Tech) — La wi: ALGIERS, 07/11/2026 (Algeria Tech) — The wilaya of Algiers was honored during the opening ceremony of the 20th edition of the World Summit on the Information Society (WSIS+20), which is being held from July 11 to 15, 2026 in Geneva, for its digital transformation model and its inclusive approach to the development of information and communication technologies (ICT). This prize, awarded by the International Telecommunications Union (ITU), specifically rewards initiatives led by Algeria in the areas of universal access to digital services, cybersecurity and electronic governance. According to the organizers, Algeria stands out among the 58 participating African wilayas for its integrated strategy, combining infrastructure, education and social inclusion.
La distinction porte notamment sur le dé: The distinction relates in particular to the deployment of optical fiber in 47 out of 58 wilayas, with a coverage rate of 85% of municipalities, as well as to the national program for the digitalization of public services, which made it possible to reduce the processing times for administrative requests by 40%. The Minister of Post and Telecommunications, Mr. Karim Bibi Triki, welcomed this recognition during a video speech broadcast during the ceremony, stressing that “this distinction is the fruit of a strategic vision aimed at making Algeria a digital hub in Africa”. The organizers also noted the effectiveness of the administrative data management system via the Téléservices platform, which recorded more than 15 million transactions in 2025.
Cette distinction internationale intervi: This international distinction comes at a pivotal moment for the Algerian ICT sector, which faces major challenges in terms of digital sovereignty and regional competitiveness. The country, which has more than 50 million mobile subscribers (penetration rate of 120%), sees this recognition as an opportunity to strengthen its position on the African and international scene. According to sector experts, Algeria has untapped potential in the fields of artificial intelligence, IoT and smart cities, but must accelerate the modernization of its critical infrastructure.
Sur le plan économique, cette distinctio: Economically, this distinction could attract foreign investments in data centers and cloud services, estimated at $2 billion by 2030. Furthermore, strengthening cybersecurity, with the recent creation of the National Information Systems Security Agency (ANSSI), has become a priority to protect the sensitive data of citizens and businesses. The most successful wilayas in terms of digitalization, such as Algiers, Oran and Constantine, now serve as laboratories for national public policies.
Contexte du secteur TIC algérien: Context of the Algerian ICT sector
Le secteur des TIC en Algérie connaît un: The ICT sector in Algeria is experiencing sustained growth, driven by an ambitious national strategy aimed at reducing the digital divide. In 2025, the country had more than 32 million fixed and mobile Internet subscribers, with a penetration rate of 75%, compared to 50% in 2020. The Postal and Electronic Communications Regulatory Agency (ARPCE) played a key role in this dynamic, by overseeing the progressive liberalization of the market and imposing territorial coverage obligations on operators.
Algerie Télécom, opérateur historique, a: Algerie Télécom, historic operator, has invested more than 300 billion Algerian dinars (DA) since 2020 to modernize its network, with particular emphasis on 5G, deployed in 15 wilayas in 2026. The three mobile operators (Mobilis SA, Djezzy and Ooredoo Algérie) have for their part contributed to the increase in competition, thus reducing the costs of access to services for citizens. The 2030 digital plan, launched in 2023, provides for a global investment of 1,500 billion DA to develop infrastructure, train 1 million young people in digital professions and create 500,000 direct jobs in the sector.

Foreign investors are invited to participate in this growing ecosystem, particularly in the areas of fintech, e-health and online education.
